subject: [PATCH v3 0/7] sched/numa: stop VMA scan filters from gating promotion

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary:
Reviewer David noted that the patch makes sense and aligns with the goal of promoting memory without bouncing, which occurs during ordinary NUMA migration.

The reviewer suggested renaming functions and variables related to memory tiering to make their purpose more explicit, specifically to clarify the relationship between sysctl_numa_balancing_mode and NUMA_BALANCING_MEMORY_TIERING.

Reviewer David (Arm) noted that Sashiko raised an issue about anonymous shared COW folios, but did not investigate further.
reviews.raw_body:
Makes sense. So in general we're happy to promote if there is no chance of
bouncing (as would happen with ordinary numa migration).

---

I wonder if a better name would just make the comment above (about memory
tiering) implicit and make more sense of the sysctl_numa_balancing_mode &
NUMA_BALANCING_MEMORY_TIERING) check.

	folio_promotable()

	folio_is_promotable()

	folio_numa_promotable()

etc.

because that seems to be what we really test with both things combined.

---

Sashiko has some comment about anonymous shared COW folios. I think it has a
point, but didn't look too closely.

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary: The author is addressing David's concern that skipping the check would allow folios to migrate between slow tiers, but Gregory explains this is a false positive because numab will only migrate to top tier and not to a slow tier.
reviews.raw_body:
its tl;dr:

`skipping this check means those folios could end up freely migrating east-west
 between slow tiers`

Which cannot happen (we only migrate to top tier, numab will never
migrate *to* a slow tier).

basically false-positive

~Gregory

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that applying the patch in tiering modes causes VMAs to become permanently stranded on lower tiers, but no fix is planned.
reviews.raw_body:
oi

Applying it in tiering modes causes VMAs to become permanently stranded
on lower tiers.

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that the patch series still needs work and will revisit it in a future version (v4), but is satisfied with the current state of patches 1-5.
reviews.raw_body:
Sounds good, i'll let this rest for a bit before spinning a v4. I think
the rest is pretty solid, but there's one other sashiko thing i need to
think about whether it's real or not.

~Gregory

reviews.author: Zi Yan
reviews.summary: Reviewer Zi Yan approved the patch by stating that folio_numab_promotable() sounds good to them.
reviews.raw_body:
folio_numab_promotable() sounds good to me.


Best Regards,
Yan, Zi

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer David pointed out an indentation issue in the patch, but overall gave a positive review stating 'LGTM' and noted that they did not check for other potential cases.
reviews.raw_body:
Indentation looks wrong.

Apart from that LGTM (did not check if there are other cases).

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer David questioned the necessity of updating placement_scan in task_numa_work(), suggesting that it could be simplified by checking if balancing is enabled and only then setting cp_flags to MM_CP_PROT_NUMA_PROMO_ONLY.

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that the placement scan filter needs to be adjusted based on the global balancing mode and VMA state, agreed to revisit the function name in a future update.

2026-09-24.patch_summary: This patch series addresses poor NUMA balancing behavior in a production deployment by modifying the VMA scan filters to no longer gate memory-tier promotion. The issue arises from the global balancing mode not being able to describe the intent of individual VMA/PTE walks, leading to unproductive socket-placement faults that prevent promotion. The patches introduce promotion-only NUMA protection walks and derive private VMA state in the folio eligibility check, allowing eligible shared folios to be promoted to a fast tier. Additionally, the patches separate VMA placement eligibility from partial-scan continuation and scan PID-inactive VMAs for promotion. The changes improve DRAM bandwidth, reduce CXL bandwidth saturation, and decrease request latency.
